# Perfo

A system performance monitor for the Omarchy bar: CPU and per-core usage, load,
memory and swap, pressure, disk I/O, network, per-port traffic, filesystems,
fan RPM and temperatures, GPU, and Intel NPU.

![Perfo](preview.png)

This repository **is** the installable `vitor.perfo` plugin. It holds only what
the plugin needs at runtime: the QML files, the manifest, and the `perfo`
binary. It is generated by the release workflow; development happens in
[VitorHolandaI/perfo-src](https://github.com/VitorHolandaI/perfo-src).

## Install

```bash
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/VitorHolandaI/perfo.git --enable
```

That is the whole installation. The binary ships inside this repository at
`bin/perfo`, and the widget resolves it relative to its own location in the
cloned plugin tree. There is nothing to put on your `PATH`, no environment
variable to set, no build step, and no privilege to grant.

## Remove

```bash
omarchy plugin disable vitor.perfo
omarchy plugin remove vitor.perfo --yes
```

## What you get

A compact bar widget with the current CPU, memory and network figures. Click it
to open the panel, which adds per-core bars, the process list with full command
lines, disk and filesystem detail, a network page with per-interface and
per-port traffic, and GPU/NPU pages when the hardware exposes them.

The same binary also runs as a standalone terminal UI and emits JSON snapshots,
but the plugin needs neither.

## Requirements

- The Omarchy shell, with Quickshell and its standard `qs.*` modules.
- Linux on x86_64. `bin/perfo` is statically linked, so no runtime library,
  package or daemon has to be installed for it.
- `/proc` and `/sys`, which is where every metric comes from.
- Optional: the NVIDIA NVML library (`libnvidia-ml.so.1`) for NVIDIA
  utilization, VRAM, temperature and power. Intel and AMD GPUs use kernel
  DRM/sysfs interfaces and need nothing extra.

## What it does not do

The monitor is read-only against `/proc` and `/sys`. It does not run as root or
ask for any privilege, does not install a service or a daemon, does not modify
your shell configuration, and contains no network client code. Session
recordings are written to disk only when you start one yourself from the panel.

## Verifying this release

`bin/perfo` is compiled by GitHub Actions in the source repository and carries a
Sigstore build provenance attestation. You can check that the binary in your
plugin directory is the one that workflow produced:

```bash
cd ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/vitor.perfo
gh attestation verify bin/perfo \
  --repo VitorHolandaI/perfo-src \
  --signer-workflow VitorHolandaI/perfo-src/.github/workflows/release.yml
```

`bundle.json` in this repository lists the SHA-256 of every published file,
including the binary.
